column1: # ALEX (alex.onb.ac.at) - HISTORISCHE RECHTS- UND GESETZESTEXTE, Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek.
# Assessed 14 September 2026, because David asked whether anything there could relate to the Lerenas.
# WHAT IT IS: about 5 million pages and 200 titles of Austrian and Habsburg official texts -
# Reichsgesetzblatt 1849-1918 in ten languages, Staatsgesetzblatt, Bundesgesetzblatt, Landesgesetz-
# blatter, stenographic parliamentary records, the Hof- und Staatshandbuch, official gazettes.
question
Does ALEX hold a Lerena?
column2: *** UNKNOWN, AND NOT DETERMINABLE TODAY. *** Its content search (/cgi-content/alex-iv.pl) returns "Suchergebnisse TOTAL (0)" together with "Diese Seite steht zur Zeit leider noch nicht zur Verfugung" for EVERY query.

column1: How that was established rather than assumed
column2: *** BY RUNNING CONTROLS. *** "Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo" each return the identical 166-byte response - TOTAL (0) plus the same unavailability notice. A term certain to appear in five million pages of Austrian law returning zero is not a null; it is a broken search.

column1: Is the search worth retrying?
column2: Yes. The title search (alex_suche.htm) works and the digitised volumes are online; it is the full-text layer that is down. This is the same failure mode this archive documented on FamilySearch two days ago, and the same rule applies: *** a zero from a search that returns zero for everything is not evidence. ***

column1: # ============ AND THE HONEST ANSWER ON RELEVANCE, INDEPENDENT OF THE OUTAGE ============
# *** THE PRIOR IS LOW. *** This family is Uruguayan, Argentine, Spanish, then South African and
# British. Nothing in four days of records touches the Habsburg lands. ALEX is a law library for a
# state this family did not live in.
# *** THE ONE REAL HOOK IS CONSULAR. *** The archive's standing open question is whether Pablo
# Armando was a Consul General, and consular appointments ARE gazetted. Austria-Hungary maintained
# consulates at Montevideo and Buenos Aires, and the Hof- und Staatshandbuch lists consuls. So:
#   - If any Lerena held an AUSTRO-HUNGARIAN honorary consulship in the River Plate, ALEX could show
#     it. That is a narrow but genuine possibility, and the family's standing - a president at a font,
#     a general, a judge, an abogado - is exactly the class from which honorary consuls were drawn.
#   - It would NOT show Pablo Armando's own claimed consulship, which was ARGENTINE and at the CAPE.
#     For that the gazette that matters is the South African one, already on this archive's list.
# *** AND A NOTE THAT BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT ARCHIVE. *** ALEX is likely to be far more use to the
# DEFRANCESKI side - Istria, Kvarner and Carniola were Habsburg territory, and Austrian gazettes and
# Landesgesetzblatter are the right body of law for them. That is this project's SIBLING archive and
# the two are kept strictly separate; recorded here only so the suggestion is not lost.
